newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish police march on parliament in pay protest.
newsitem.headline: Irish police march on parliament in pay protest.

text.p: About one thousand off-duty Irish police officers marched on parliament on Wednesday in an unprecedented protest over pay.

The acting General Secretary of the Garda (police) Representatives Association complained there had been no government probe into police pay since 1979 and that police were not enjoying the fruits of an economic boom.
The marchers handed a letter to Prime Minister John Bruton calling for a review to put police on a par with other government officials such as customs and excise workers.
Police say they are around 3,000 Irish pounds ($4,620) behind comparable government jobs and some 7,000 behind British police across the Irish sea.
Bruton told parliament that police pay would be examined in a review of efficiency and staffing, which is due to be completed shortly.
The GRA has around 6,000 members out of the 10,000-strong force. Police are not allowed to join a trade union and are not covered by national agreements between employers, unions and the government.
